notes.meaning: The Holy Spirit prompted Simeon to go into the temple courts at the exact right moment. Meanwhile, Joseph and Mary brought the infant Jesus to fulfill the requirements of the Law of Moses for a firstborn son. God's timing brought together the waiting prophet and the young family.

When Simeon saw the child, he took Jesus gently into his arms and praised God with great joy. The Spirit made it clear to him that this humble baby was the promised Savior. True faith recognized God's glory in a helpless infant.

Simeon told God that he was now ready to die in complete peace because God had kept His word. He spoke as a faithful servant whose long watch of waiting for the Messiah was finally over. When believers see God fulfill His promises in Christ, they can face death without fear.

Simeon declared that his own physical eyes had now seen the salvation provided by God. He called Jesus salvation because this child was the Savior who would rescue His people. His physical sight confirmed the spiritual hope he had carried in his heart for years.

God prepared this salvation openly where every nation could see it. It was not planned in secret for only a few, but set before the whole world like a great feast. God invites all peoples to look to Jesus and be saved.

Simeon praised Jesus as a light that brings revelation to the Gentiles, who had lived without God's word. At the same time, Jesus is the greatest honor of Israel, fulfilling the promises made to the Jewish people. God's mercy extends to all nations while honoring His covenant with Israel.

Joseph and Mary were filled with wonder as they listened to what Simeon said about the child. Even though they already knew Jesus was miraculous, these broad promises about the whole world brought fresh awe. Good parents continue to marvel at how God works through Christ.

Simeon blessed the parents and warned Mary that Jesus would divide the people of Israel. Some would stumble and fall in ruin through their unbelief, while others would rise to new spiritual life by trusting Him. Jesus would also face fierce opposition from those who rejected God's truth.

differ.view: Christ was appointed for the fall of the non-elect who reject Him and the rising of the elect who are granted faith to believe.

notes.meaning: Simeon told Mary that Jesus' ministry would expose the hidden thoughts of human hearts, revealing who truly loved God. He also foretold that a sword would pierce Mary's own soul, pointing to the deep sorrow she would endure when her Son was rejected and killed. Walking with Christ brings great blessing, but it can also involve deep grief.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: This sword prophecy is seen as the earliest announcement of Christ's passion, fulfilled when Mary stood at the foot of the cross suffering alongside her crucified Son.

notes.meaning: Luke introduces Anna, an elderly prophetess from the northern tribe of Asher. She had lived with her husband for only seven years before becoming a widow. Her presence showed that God still kept a faithful remnant and restored the gift of prophecy at Christ's coming.

Anna lived as a widow until she was eighty-four years old, spending all her time around the temple courts. She devoted her life entirely to God through constant prayer and regular fasting. Her lifelong faithfulness provides a wonderful example of honoring God in old age.

Arriving just as Simeon was speaking, Anna immediately began thanking God for sending the Savior. She then shared the good news about Jesus with everyone in Jerusalem who was eagerly waiting for God's redemption. God used this godly woman as one of the first witnesses to declare that the Messiah had arrived.

After Joseph and Mary fulfilled every ceremony required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to their home in Nazareth in Galilee. They faithfully obeyed God's commands at every step. Their quiet return home shows that God's great work often continues in ordinary, everyday life.

As Jesus grew up, His body gained strength and His human mind was continuously filled with wisdom. God's special favor and blessing rested visibly upon Him. His normal childhood development proves that the Son of God was truly human in every way.

Every year, Joseph and Mary traveled to Jerusalem to celebrate the Passover festival, which remembered God freeing Israel from Egypt. While the Law only required men to attend, Mary gladly went along as part of their family's regular worship. Their godly habits created a home centered on honoring the Lord.

When Jesus reached twelve years of age, His parents brought Him along to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast. At twelve, Jewish boys were trained more closely in the Law and prepared for adult religious duties. Jesus was raised to participate fully in the worship of God's covenant people.

When the full days of the feast ended and the pilgrims started heading home, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. His parents did not know He remained there. Accustomed to His good judgment and obedience, they did not suspect anything was amiss.

Because people traveled from the feast in large caravans of neighbors and kin, Joseph and Mary assumed Jesus was walking with other travelers. They went a full day's journey before looking for Him among their relatives and friends. In such a large crowd, it was easy to believe He was safe with others.

When Joseph and Mary realized Jesus was nowhere in the caravan, they turned around and hurried back to Jerusalem to search for Him. Their hearts were filled with deep worry and grief over the missing boy. They did not stop until they retraced their steps to find Him.

On the third day after leaving Jerusalem, His parents finally discovered Jesus in the temple courts. He was sitting among the respected Jewish teachers, listening closely to their words and asking them questions. Jesus took the humble position of an eager student of God's Word.

Everyone who listened to the twelve-year-old Jesus was astonished by His deep understanding and His thoughtful answers. His grasp of the Scriptures went far beyond His years. Even as a boy, Jesus showed glimpses of the divine wisdom that would mark His future ministry.

When Joseph and Mary saw Him among the teachers, they were amazed, and Mary asked why He had caused them so much worry. She explained that she and Joseph, His earthly father, had been frantically searching for Him in deep distress. Her reaction expressed the natural relief and pain of a loving parent.

Jesus gently asked His parents why they had to search for Him, asking if they did not know He had to be in His Father's house. These are the very first recorded words of Jesus, showing He already understood His unique bond with God. He made it clear that His duty to His heavenly Father came before all human ties.

differ.view: Jesus asked why they searched anywhere else when He naturally had to be in His Father's house, pointing to His location in the temple.
Jesus said He must be about His Father's business, which points beyond the temple building to the whole work and mission God gave Him to do.

notes.meaning: Joseph and Mary did not fully grasp what Jesus meant by His answer. Even though they had witnessed miracles surrounding His birth, they still struggled to understand the full scope of His divine mission. God's ways are often deeper and grander than human minds can take in at the time.

Jesus returned with His parents down to Nazareth and lived in willing obedience to their authority. Even though He was the Son of God, He showed perfect honor to His earthly parents by submitting to their guidance and learning a trade. Mary kept all these remarkable events in her memory, thinking on them often.

Jesus continued to grow physically in body, and mentally and spiritually in wisdom. His pure character and loving life brought great pleasure to God and won the warm respect of people around Him. In His human nature, Jesus lived out the perfect model of a godly life growing toward maturity.
